newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Zurich to buy Scudder in $2.4 billion deal.
newsitem.headline: Zurich to buy Scudder in $2.4 billion deal.

text.p: Zurich Group, Switzerland's biggest insurance company, said Friday it agreed to buy Scudder, Stevens & Clark, the U.S. asset management and mutual fund company, in a deal worth about $2.4 billion.

The transaction will combine Zurich Group's Chicago-based Zurich Kemper Investments Inc. unit, which has $80 billion in assets under management, with privately held Scudder's $120 billion mutual fund and asset management business.

The move, Zurich's second major purchase of an investment firm in less than two years, highlights its determination to be a force in investment management in the United States, which accounts for 45 percent of the world's investment assets.
"With Scudder we have reached the critical mass in an extremely important market," Zurich Chief Executive Rolf Hueppi said at a news conference.

He said the deal could also unlock potential in Europe, which does not have as strong a stock ownership culture as the United States but is seeing a shift from state-funded pension plans to private pension plans.

Hueppi said the acquisition would be slightly dilutive to earnings in 1998, turning neutral in 1999. He estimated that writeoffs related to the purchase would total $30 million to $40 million over the next 20 years or so.

Zurich, which completed its acquisition of Kemper in January 1996, said its corporate strategy was to offer "tailored solutions for financial protection and investment management." It has been actively expanding in both asset management and reinsurance.

Analysts said the combination was ideal since 70 percent to 80 percent of Kemper's business is in retail mutual funds, while about two-thirds of the business at Scudder, which is based in New York, is done with institutions.

The acquisition also provides Kemper with Scudder's direct distribution capabilities and clients, along with greater exposure in the faster-growing equity fund and international fund business segments.
More than 80 percent of Kemper's business is in fixed income and money market funds, a segment not growing very quickly, analysts said.
"Strategically this makes sense, of course, but we don't yet know about the underlying profitability of Scudder," said UBS insurance analyst Thomas Kalbermatten.
